ACKS-LIB.settings.sheetTheme.name: Character-sheet theme
ACKS-LIB.settings.sheetTheme.hint: Style the ACKS windows like the printed ACKS II character sheet: burgundy banners with small-caps lettering, gray sheet, white boxed fields. Per player.

ACKS-LIB.settings.manageVision.name: Token vision from ACKS senses
ACKS-LIB.settings.manageVision.hint: Set each token's sight from its sheet: ordinary eyes see only what is lit, lightless vision and a thief's shadowy senses see their own radius as dim light, and night vision brightens dim light without piercing true dark. Also emits light from a lit torch, lantern or candle the character carries. Edit a token's vision by hand and this leaves that token alone from then on.

enforceMode.name: Equip-limit enforcement
enforceMode.hint: How to handle RAW-illegal equip attempts (too many hands, a second armour suit, a shield with no free hand).

proficiencyEnforcement.name: Proficiency penalties
proficiencyEnforcement.hint: Whether weapon, armour, and fighting-style proficiency PENALTIES are enforced (Non-Proficient Use, RR p. 106). Positive facts from ACKS Abilities characters — Weapon Finesse, a Specialization's style, Martial/Armour Training picks, Weapon Focus — always apply through the bridge regardless of this setting. Always enforce treats this module's flags as authoritative: configure each character with its ACKS Class Training items (a fighting style plus weapon/armour lists) and the gate is correct. Automatic instead keeps penalties off while ACKS Abilities is active, for worlds where characters rely on it for their base proficiency lists (which its model cannot yet express, so absence of a fact must not read as untrained).
proficiencyEnforcement.auto: Automatic — penalties off while ACKS Abilities is active; bridged bonuses still apply
proficiencyEnforcement.on: Always enforce — this module's flags are authoritative (default; configure characters via the ACKS Class Training compendium)
proficiencyEnforcement.off: Never enforce (equip limits, styles, and bridged bonuses still apply)

rollAutomation.name: Automate attack/damage rolls
rollAutomation.hint: Inject RAW fighting-style and proficiency modifiers into attack and damage rolls (Weapon Finesse, dual-wield, two-handed damage, Weapon Focus, Precise Shooting, non-proficiency). Requires libWrapper. Turn off to apply only always-on bonuses via the loadout effect.

defaultHandBudget.hint: Number of hands a humanoid actor has for wielding weapons and shields. Raised per-actor by the Four Arms power or monster anatomy effects.

overlayShieldVariants.name: Overlay: shield variants (JJ)
overlayShieldVariants.hint: Buckler, auxiliary, crescent, heater, kite, and phalanx shields with strap positions and vulnerable rules. Judges Journal pp. 407–408.

overlayManeuvers.name: Overlay: combat maneuvers
overlayManeuvers.hint: Special-maneuver helpers (disarm, knock down, wrestle, sunder, etc.) aware of Combat Trickery and weapon qualities. Revised Rulebook pp. 305–306.

overlayItemLoss.name: Overlay: item loss from damage (JJ)
overlayItemLoss.hint: Destroy carried equipment on heavy area damage. Judges Journal p. 398.

overlayMounted.name: Overlay: mounted saves
overlayMounted.hint: Paralysis saves to stay mounted without a military saddle / Mounted Combat or Riding. Revised Rulebook p. 308.

overlayNamed.name: Overlay: named magic items (JJ)
overlayNamed.hint: Named arms and armour that unlock bonuses by level. Judges Journal p. 399.

overlayScavenged.name: Overlay: scavenged equipment (RR)
overlayScavenged.hint: Condition tables for salvaged gear. Revised Rulebook p. 160.

overlayBeastman.name: Overlay: beastman gear (MM)
overlayBeastman.hint: Barbed armour, blasting-fire bombs, dread banners, and other beastman equipment. Monstrous Manual pp. 55–57.

overlayEnclosingHelm.name: Overlay: enclosing helmet
overlayEnclosingHelm.hint: Heavy helmets impose −1 to surprise rolls and −4 to Listening but grant +2 on Mortal Wounds. Revised Rulebook p. 128.

ammoTracking.name: Track ammunition & thrown weapons
ammoTracking.hint: On a missile attack, decrement the matching ammunition (arrows/bolts/stones) or the thrown weapon by one. A single thrown weapon (hand axe, javelin) is marked as thrown — unequipped and weightless until recovered — rather than destroyed. Recovery is manual (Recover Thrown Weapons macro); RAW specifies no automatic recovery. Requires libWrapper.

app.title: Exploration Formation
app.addSelectedHint: Add the tokens selected on the canvas to this formation (their tokens are stashed and replaced by the party token)

app.disbandConfirm: Disband {name}? Member tokens will be restored around the party token.

app.shieldHint: Close/open the lantern shutter: sheds no light while closed but keeps burning oil (RR equipment). Mapping needs an open light.
app.frontageHint: How many march abreast (RR p. 264: single file in corridors 5' or narrower, two columns at 6'+). Groups the list into ranks and shapes combat deployment; the party token itself stays 1×1.
app.autoArrangeHint: Build an I-formation per RR p. 264: a FULL front line (scouts and best-armored melee, spears next) and a FULL back line (Rear Guard, then missile users) are staffed first; non-combatants, the mapper, and spellcasters hold the middle ranks, centered with blank slots. app.emptyState: No formation yet — right-click a token and use "Add to party", or create a Party Formation actor.
app.speedHint: The party moves at the pace of its slowest member (feet per 10-minute turn)
app.carryHint: Distance moved that has not yet added up to a full turn
app.advanceTurnHint: Mark off one full dungeon turn (10 minutes) — methodical searching, picking locks methodically, and other full-turn activities
app.restTurnHint: Spend one turn resting (resets the rest counter and removes Winded)
app.encounterNowHint: Make a wandering-monster throw right now (GM-whispered)
app.rationsHint: Consume one ration per member from their inventory
app.undoTurnHint: Roll the clock back one turn (bookkeeping only; world time is not rewound)
app.pauseHint: Pause/resume movement-driven turn tracking (e.g. while repositioning the token)
app.noStashedToken: No stashed token: this member was added without a canvas token and will not be re-placed on disband
app.removeMemberHint: Remove from the formation and restore their token beside the party token
app.toggleLightHint: Extinguish or relight (remaining burn time is kept; relighting takes a round via the tinderbox)
app.tableHint: Default RollTable drawn from when a wandering-monster encounter triggers. An ACKS Encounter Zone region under the party token overrides this.
app.spellPickHint: Track a spell known by a member (duration parsed from the spell when it reads like "6 turns")
app.trackSpellHint: Counts down one per dungeon turn; announced when it gutters (1 turn) and expires
app.spellPlusHint: Add one turn (e.g. higher caster level)

app.saveTooltip: Roll a {save} saving throw for every member against their own sheet's target
app.detachedBadge: Out ahead of the party on their own token
app.detachHint: Detach: step out of the party token onto your own, carrying your own light and seeing with your own eyes. You stay in the formation — turns, rest and encounters keep counting. You may range one round's movement ahead, then must wait for the party to catch up.
app.recallHint: Rejoin the party token, bringing back everything that happened while you were out
app.darkSightHint: How far this character sees with no light at all (lightless vision, or a thief's shadowy senses). Everyone else sees only what a light source reveals.

app.orphanParty: This party actor is not linked to any formation.

app.advanceRoundHint: Mark off one bookkeeping round (1 minute; 10 per turn) — hasty actions like listening, hasty searching, bashing a door, or lighting a torch

A drawn map of {scene}.

Its recorded territory is stored on this item. When the party can match it to their surroundings, the Judge anchors it from the party sheet to reveal the mapped area.

A working map of {scene}, drawn in the field by {mapper}.

The recorded exploration is stored on this item and updates each dungeon turn. Whoever holds it holds the map: trade or loot it freely. When the party can match it to their surroundings, the Judge anchors it from the party sheet to reveal its territory.

map.reasonScene: This map depicts a different scene than the party's
map.reasonViewing: View the party's scene to anchor (the fog texture only exists for the viewed scene)
map.statusLine: Working record updated at turn {turns} of exploring {scene}. The drawn map itself is stored on this item — carry, sell, or loot it; a Judge can Anchor it from the party sheet to reveal its territory.

rolls.listenHint: 1 round (marked off). Every member rolls Listening with their own sheet target. RAW: only the closest member's result applies; once per turn while moving.
rolls.listenNote: Only the member closest to the sound may apply their result (RR p. 265). Once per turn while the party is moving.

rolls.searchHastyHint: 1 round (marked off). Only members with a Searching skill may hastily search — Adventuring is not permitted (RR p. 265).

rolls.searchMethodicalHint: Takes 1 full turn (advanced automatically). Skill users roll at +4; anyone else uses their Adventuring target (18+).
rolls.searchMethodicalNote: 1 turn (10 minutes, marked off automatically), 5' reach (10' with pole). May be repeated.
rolls.bashHint: 1 round (marked off). Dungeonbashing with ±4 per point of STR modifier (crowbar +2 and size modifiers applied by the Judge).

rolls.nobodyCapable: No member can attempt {check} (no matching skill on any sheet).

rolls.trackingNote: 1 turn (10 minutes, marked off automatically). On a failure the area cannot be searched for tracks again for one hour. Judge modifiers: +2/+4/+6/+8 by group size, +4 soft ground, -8 rocky, -1 per 12h of weather, -4 per hour of rain/snow, -4 dim light.
rolls.noHastyHurried: The party is hurrying at combat speed — hasty searching is not possible (RR p. 263). Slow to a careful pace first.

role.noncombatantHint: Stays with the party token when combat begins and is not added to the initiative tracker
role.carrierHint: Carries the down: the carried count as 7 3/6 stone plus half their equipment (the rescue rule), split evenly among Carriers — the load slows the carriers' pace and therefore the party's

winded.effectDescription: Cannot charge or run until resting for 1 turn (10 minutes). ACKS II RR p. 271.

chat.windedStatus: The party is WINDED — no charging or running until it rests 1 turn
chat.becameWinded: More than 5 turns without rest — the party is now winded!
chat.restedRecovered: The party has rested and is no longer winded.
chat.lightGuttering: {bearer}'s {light} is guttering — one turn of light remains!
chat.dayPassed: A full day of delve time has passed — consume rations and check spell recovery.
chat.encounterDetail: Maximum encounter distance {distance}' (2d6×10). Occurs at minute {minute} of the turn (1d10). Roll on the dungeon's encounter table and follow the encounter procedure (distance → reactions → surprise).
chat.fogLost: With no one mapping, the party's map of {scene} fades — the fog of war closes back in. Assign a Mapper (with a lit light source) to keep explored areas revealed.
chat.fogRestored: The mapper takes up the quill — explored areas of {scene} stay revealed on the map.
chat.detached: {name} moves out ahead of the party.
chat.combatDeployed: The formation breaks for battle — {n} member(s) deployed to the combat tracker.
chat.combatReformed: Combat over ({rounds} round(s)) — the party reforms into formation.
chat.combatFallen: Down and gathered up with the party: {names}. Assign Carriers to bring them along, or remove them from the formation to abandon them where they fell.
chat.combatNoCombatants: No deployable members (all non-combatants or without tokens) — party token left in the tracker.
chat.bigMove: That drag consumed {turns} turns. If that was repositioning rather than exploration, use the undo-turn button or pause tracking.
chat.hurriedStatus: Hurrying at combat speed: much more noise (earshot as walking/talking or worse), no mapping, no 10' poles, no hasty searching (RR p. 263)
chat.encounterNow: The wandering monsters arrive at minute {minute} of the turn — interrupt the party's movement here and run the encounter.
chat.signature: Party signature: {light}, {noise} — applies to surprise and earshot (RR pp. 265–266)

warnings.inCombat: Members are deployed for combat — the party reforms automatically when the combat ends.
warnings.noMapper: No mapper assigned — without a map the party risks getting lost (assign the Mapper role).
warnings.mapperNoLight: The mapper has no lit light source — mapping requires bright light.
warnings.mapperNoProficiency: The mapper lacks the Mapping proficiency — the Judge gives only vague measurements and the mapper cannot passively notice map errors (RR p. 264).
warnings.noLight: No lit light source — the party cannot see (unless members have shadowy senses or lightless vision).
warnings.winded: Winded: the party cannot charge or run until it rests for 1 turn.
warnings.restDue: 5 turns without rest — the party must rest 1 turn now or become winded.
warnings.poleNoItem: {name} has the 10' Pole role but no pole or polearm in inventory.
warnings.downNoCarrier: DOWN with no Carriers: {names} — the party cannot bring them along (assign the Carrier role, or remove them from the formation to abandon them).
warnings.carrying: Carrying {names}: {stone} stone total, split among {carriers} Carrier(s) ({share} st each) — carrier pace is recomputed with the load.
warnings.darkBlinded: Darkness: {blinded} cannot see and move at 1/3 speed (blinded). Seeing in the dark: {sighted}.
warnings.darkSighted: Darkness: the whole party operates on dark senses ({sighted}). No mapping or reading without bright light.

hud.addToParty: Add to party (adds all controlled tokens; creates a formation if the scene has none)

warn.noFormationYet: No formation exists yet — right-click a token and use "Add to party", or create a Party Formation actor.
warn.duplicatePartyToken: This formation already has a party token on the canvas — delete it first to re-place the party.
warn.overburdened: Party exploration speed is 0 — someone is overburdened!
warn.spellNeedsName: Pick a spell or enter a name to track.
warn.spellNeedsTurns: Enter a duration in turns (the spell's duration couldn't be parsed).
warn.noPoleItem: {name} has no pole or polearm in inventory — the 10' Pole role needs the physical implement.
warn.noFreeHand: {bearer} has no free hand to hold a light — sheathe or stow something to carry it properly.

partyTokenImage.name: Party token image
partyTokenImage.hint: Image used for the party token and party actor.

playersMoveParty.name: All players can move the party token
playersMoveParty.hint: Coarse override: grants every player owner rights on party actors. Normally unnecessary — players who own a member of a formation automatically get vision through, and control of, its party token.

advanceWorldTime.name: Advance world time
advanceWorldTime.hint: Advance the Foundry world clock by 10 minutes per dungeon turn (keeps Active Effect durations and calendar modules in sync).

publicTurnCards.name: Public turn summaries
publicTurnCards.hint: Post the per-turn summary card publicly. Wandering-monster throws are always GM-whispered. Disable to whisper everything to the GM.

lightItemEnforcement.name: Light-source equipment
lightItemEnforcement.hint: Whether lighting a torch/candle/lantern requires the bearer to carry it (a lantern needs the lantern plus a flask of oil). When enforced, the fuel is consumed (the torch/candle, or a lantern's oil).

encounterEvery.name: Wandering monster throw frequency (turns)
encounterEvery.hint: Make an encounter throw every N dungeon turns. RAW: 2. Set 0 to disable automatic throws.

encounterTarget.name: Wandering monster target value
encounterTarget.hint: Encounter occurs on this value or higher on 1d6. RAW: 6.

manageFog.name: Tie fog of war to the mapper
manageFog.hint: Fog exploration on a scene is fully disabled — neither shown nor recorded — unless a formation there has a member with the Mapper role. Current vision still shows. The scene's original fog mode is restored when the formation leaves or disbands. Scenes whose fog was already off are left alone.

mapperNeedsLight.name: Mapper requires a lit light source
mapperNeedsLight.hint: Per the rules, mapping requires bright light. When enabled, the map (fog exploration) is only retained while the formation also has a lit torch, lantern, or candle.

syncTokenLight.name: Party token emits light
syncTokenLight.hint: The party token automatically emits the brightest lit light source's light (torch/lantern 15'/30', candle 5'/10'), so players can see where they are even without a mapper.

fuzzMeasurement.name: Fuzz player measurements without a proficient mapper
fuzzMeasurement.hint: On scenes where the formation's mapper lacks Mapping proficiency, players' ruler and drag distances show a hidden consistent error (~×0.8–1.25, rounded to the grid); with no working mapper at all they show "?". GMs always see true values. Players can still count grid squares — this is a deterrent, not a lock.

signalAffectsEncounters.name: Light & noise modify encounter throws (optional)
signalAffectsEncounters.hint: NOT in the reference extracts (light/noise affect surprise and earshot per RR pp. 265-266; the encounter-rate rule, if any, is in the encounter chapter). When enabled: hurried parties +1 on the 1d6 throw, dark and careful parties -1. Off = RAW-as-extracted.

audit.title: Skill Audit
audit.openHint: Skill audit: see exactly how each party roll resolves per member, and flag custom skill items
audit.hint: How each party roll resolves for every member — the item or Adventuring target used, auto-scaled level, and bonuses. Rolls always use these live values.
audit.itemsHint: Flag ANY ability item to participate in a party roll (Used for), auto-scale on a thief progression, or scale at a fraction of the owner's level (e.g. 0.5 = as a thief of half class level). Unflagged items match by name and use their sheet target.
audit.throwBonusHint: Flat adjustment to this item's party-roll throw: +4 makes the target 4 lower (e.g. Lockpicking Expertise's bonus applied to a skill). Leave 0 for none.
audit.importedTarget: Imported target (from the book's own ladder)
audit.inferredProgression: Progression inferred from the imported identity ({key}) — no binding needed.
audit.progressionNotImported: Bound to "{key}", but that skill has not been imported into this world — there is no ladder to scale with, so the sheet target below is used. Import the skill with acks-content to restore auto-scaling.
audit.tableHint: Auto-scaled targets come from these rows at ceil(level × factor). The rows are read from your own books at import — import skills with acks-content to populate this.
audit.tabNotSkill: Not flagged as a party-roll skill. Set "Used for" to make this item participate in a party roll.
audit.isSkillHint: Mark this proficiency as a skill for party rolls. Turns on the Skill tab showing its progression, level factor, and live resolved target.
audit.effectiveRow: {name} is level {level}; ×{factor} factor → progression row L{row}.
audit.rosterHint: Every distinct ability in the party, once. Automation matches by capability, explicit binding, or name — the union of all three. Click a ruling to force it off or on; the reset returns everything to automatic. Rulings are world-wide and keyed to the ability, so one decision covers every copy.
audit.resetHint: Clear every GM ruling and let automation decide again.
audit.resetConfirm: Clear all ability rulings and return every ability to automatic detection?
audit.overridden: Set by the GM — not automatic.
audit.toggleHint: Click to cycle: automatic → forced off → forced on → automatic.

route.binding: Bound explicitly on the item's Skill tab.
route.name: Matched by NAME only — this breaks if the item is renamed, and is the likeliest false positive. Bind it on the item's Skill tab to make it durable.

ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.created: Posting created: {total} candidate(s) this month. Week-1 search fee: {fee} gp.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.commissionedHint: Pay the full month's fee to spread the word: rolls as one rarity lower, re-rolled each month (JJ 119).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.domainRulerHint: Domain rulers may hire henchmen of any level below their own (RR 168).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.presentedLevelHint: RR 168: candidates judge an employer by appearance and living expenses — how much they truly know before signing on is the Judge's call, so you may present as another level. The hiring cap uses the level they BELIEVE; if a hireling later concludes the truth, the loyalty roll takes −1 per level of difference (auto-applied, GM-overridable).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.liedLevel: GM only: employer presented as level
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.weekHint: Week of the current availability month. ½ of the pool arrives in week 1, ¼ in week 2, the rest in week 3 (RR 162).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.poolHint: Availability is rolled once per game month per specification. Hover a row for the roll detail.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.toggleDetails: Toggle whether players see this posting's candidate details
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.none: No recruitment postings. Pay the weekly search fee to post notices, carouse, and canvass the guilds.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.levelCapError: {employer} cannot hire level {level} henchmen (cap: level {cap}, RR 168).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.classLevelHint: Leave level blank to search by class alone; naming the level narrows the search (+1 rarity per level above 1st) and replaces only that level's rolled henchmen.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.duplicate-sp: That specification was already searched this month (once per month per specification, JJ 118).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.duplicate-se: That hiring character already has an active search for this hireling type here — the market's pool is shared (RR 162).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.privateHint: Private specific search (JJ 118): paid and rolled separately for this recruiter.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.criteriaHint: Pick what you are paying to see: the general henchman market, a mercenary or specialist type — or a directed search that replaces rolled henchmen with what you seek.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.criteria-req: A post must name what you are looking for — a class, proficiency, troop or specialist type.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.level-requir: A leveled search must name the level — it sets the price.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.not-yours: You can only post on behalf of a character you own.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.submitted: Posting submitted — the GM client rolls the search.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.advertVeteranHint: Advertised a full month — upgraded to a COMMISSION: its rolls shift one rarity toward common while the post stays up.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.market.hint: Availability belongs to the town (RR 162): each hireling type is rolled once per game month at the location's market class and shared by every recruiter. Postings are paid searches that access it.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.market.empty: Nothing rolled this month. Create a posting to canvass the market.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.demographicsHint: Weighted culture mix used to generate candidate names, ages, and appearances (RR 495-503). Empty = uniform random.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixDropHint: Drop a RollTable of cultures here to set this town's culture mix (result text = culture, weight = share).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixExport: Export the culture mix as a RollTable (prefilled) — tweak it, then drop it back here.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixTableHint: Culture mix for a settlement. Tweak entries/weights, then drop this table onto the location sheet's demographics block to apply.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixExported: Culture mix exported as "{name}" — tweak and drop it back on the sheet.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixNoCultures: "{name}" has no recognizable culture entries — result text must be a culture name or id.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.demographicsEmpty: No demographics set — candidates draw from all cultures evenly.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.migration.wiped: acks-henchmen: location "{name}" was migrated to the shared-market model (v0.3.0) — its old test postings/candidates were cleared.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.repair.swept: acks-henchmen: repaired dangling hireling references on {count} actor(s) — deleted hirelings were still listed on their employers (this crashed character sheets).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.setting.autoRepairReferenc: At world load, remove references to deleted hirelings from employers' rosters. A dangling reference crashes character-sheet rendering in acks 14.0.1. Turn off only if you repair manually with the "Repair Henchmen References" macro.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.tablesMissing: acks-henchmen: rules tables not installed ({list}). Book tables are no longer shipped — they will be imported per-world from your own ACKS II PDFs (import path in development). Market, wage, and hiring automation stays disabled until then.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.unknown-clas: That class is not in the location's rarity table.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.past-legenda: Rarer than Legendary — not findable by this method (JJ 119).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.socket.noGm: A GM must be connected to complete recruitment.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.candidate.name: Candidate
ACKS-HENCHMEN.candidate.recruit: Attempt to recruit (Reaction to Hiring Offer)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.candidate.none: No candidates. Create a posting and advance time to draw them in.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.cond.threats: when threatening; targets <5 HD or outnumbered (Intimidation)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.cond.ownSettlement: with 0th-level locals of the home settlement
ACKS-HENCHMEN.cond.related: if related by blood or marriage
ACKS-HENCHMEN.cond.witnessed: when deeds are witnessed and recorded
ACKS-HENCHMEN.cond.sameReligion: hirelings of the same religion, when present
ACKS-HENCHMEN.mod.signingBonusHint: Paid on acceptance; Bribery proficiency cheapens the tiers
ACKS-HENCHMEN.mod.previousRefusalsHint: Cumulative −1 per prior attempt the candidate rejected (RR 162)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.mod.slanderHint: −1 per refuse-and-slander result against the party here (RR 162)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.mod.monsterMoraleHint: Independent monster: its own morale; defeated group: its previous leader's (MM 351)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.mod.effectiveLoyaltyHint: Base + permanent adjustments + employer CHA and powers
ACKS-HENCHMEN.mod.apparentLevelDiffHint: −1 per level the hireling believes he exceeds his employer (RR 168)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.mod.recentCasualties: Henchmen lost in the last month/adventure (−1)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.mod.riskShared: Similar risk to what others face
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.refuseSlander: All further reaction rolls by this party in this town/region suffer −1; this NPC can never be recruited by the party.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.tryAgain: Reluctant — sweeten the deal (more pay, a magic item…) for another roll, else treat as Refuse.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.acceptElan: Accepted in very good spirit: +1 to the hireling's loyalty score.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.betrayal: Feigns acceptance to betray the adventurer when opportunity arises.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.escape: Feigns acceptance to save its life; deserts at the first safe opportunity.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.hesitate: Accepts with uncertain loyalties: starts at loyalty −2 instead of 0.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.hostility: Leaves service immediately; considers the employer a rival and enemy; can never be re-hired.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.resignation: Leaves service immediately, without ill will; could be recruited again later.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.fanatic: A dedicated, sworn servant: loyalty score +1 (permanent).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.refuses: Unwilling to follow orders. If the employer insists: −1 permanent loyalty, then roll again.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.outcomeHint.begrudging: Complies with minimum enthusiasm: −1 to related loyalty rolls or proficiency throws; quits early unless ordered on.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.throwUi.secretHint: The Judge rolls secretly: the result is whispered to the GM (RR 166).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.throwUi.gmOnlyOverride: Only the GM can unlock derived modifiers.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.name: Settlement name
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.sourceDefault: Default (Class IV) — set urban families or an override
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.alignmentHint: Directed searches for opposed-alignment classes shift one rarity step (chaotic warlocks hide in lawful towns). The default class ladders assume a lawful settlement — use a rarity-table variant to re-ladder other alignments.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.slanderHint: Each refuse-and-slander result gives the party −1 on further reaction rolls in this town/region (RR 162).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.marketLogHint: What the market did and when — the rollback record if the clock gets adjusted.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.processNowHint: Materialize due arrivals, charge due weekly fees, roll the month over if due.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.reloadHint: Re-load the imported rules tables from world data (no book needed) and refresh the board — recovers a market that reads empty because of a display glitch, not because it is genuinely empty. Does not roll the market; that is Process time.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.reloaded: Reloaded {layers} table set(s) from world data and refreshed.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.reloadNoTables: No rules tables are stored in this world — a GM must import them from a connected book (they persist afterward).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.advanceWeekHint: Advances the world clock 7 days (all postings age).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.special.hint: The results of DIRECTED searches (specific class / proficiency, JJ 118) sit here until hired or the month re-rolls, alongside notable NPCs: drag an actor onto this sheet to list one (no time limit unless set via the hourglass). Hiring attempts are tracked per NPC everywhere.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.special.refusalsHint: Failed hiring attempts by this party against this NPC — each adds a cumulative −1 to further offers (RR 162).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.special.added: {name} is now available for hire here.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.special.empty: None. Drag an actor here, or found recruits will appear when registered.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.recruit.pickEmployer: Who is making the hiring offer?
ACKS-HENCHMEN.recruit.notAvailable: That candidate has not arrived yet (or is no longer available).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.recruit.slanderedBlock: That NPC refused and slandered the party — no further attempts are possible (RR 162).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.recruit.info: Offering employment to {name} (wage {wage} gp/month). Bribery proficiency: {bribery}.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.recruit.tryAgainChat: The candidate is reluctant. {employer} must sweeten the deal (better pay, a magic item…) to earn another roll — otherwise it counts as a refusal.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.hire.limitReached: {name} already leads {count} of {max} henchmen — hiring more will cost an existing henchman (RR 168).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.hire.hiredChat: {name} enters the service of {employer} at {wage} gp/month plus a half share of treasure.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.hire.error.limit: Henchman limit reached (blocked by world setting).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.group.hireHint: Assemble available troops (and an officer) into one stacked unit actor instead of a lone actor each.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.group.hireTitle: Hire a Unit as a Group
ACKS-HENCHMEN.group.forEmployer: Assembling a unit for {name}. Troops become counted stacks; an officer is hired and linked as commander.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.group.hireFailed: Could not hire as a group ({reason}).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.group.noEmployer: No employer available to hire for.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.group.noneAvailable: No troops or officers are available in the market to form a group.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.group.overCommand: This unit ({strength} infantry-equivalents) is larger than its officer can personally lead (RR 169 limit {cap}). Hire a higher-rank officer, or split it — a force of several platoons is an army (acks-troops), not a skirmish unit.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.unitMorale.title: Unit Morale (2d6)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.unitMorale.base: {name} — base morale {base} (troop type, officer, and leader modifiers). Tick what applies:
ACKS-HENCHMEN.gold.noCoins: {name} has no money items to credit.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.setting.wagesToBankHint: Wages credit each hireling's banked coin (quantitybank); disable to hand over carried coin instead.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.searchFeeHint: Rolled weekly per hireling type searched (RR 162), at this town's market class — the same rate for every recruiter.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.time.advanceDisabled: World-time advancement is disabled in the module settings.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.hire.queuedChat: {employer} sealed the deal — the recruit is reserved and their character sheet will be drawn up when a GM next connects.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.hire.error.actor-create-de: This seat cannot create the hireling's actor — the hire was queued for the next GM connection.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.card.calamityBody: {note} — a Hireling Loyalty roll is required (RR 166). The Judge rolls secretly and may adjust ±2.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.card.calamitySkip: Calamity recorded for {name} ({note}) — this hireling does not make loyalty rolls on calamities.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.card.waived: Loyalty roll waived by the Judge
ACKS-HENCHMEN.card.levelGainBody: {name} reached level {level} in service: loyalty +1 recorded. A Hireling Loyalty roll is due (RR 166).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.card.refusesBody: If the employer insists: −1 permanent loyalty, then roll Obedience again (RR 167).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.wage.nothingDue: No wages are due for {name}'s hirelings.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.wage.dueBody: {count} hireling(s)/unit(s) are owed wages — {total} gp total. Missing wages is a calamity (RR 166).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.title: Hirelings of {name}
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.allCardsHint: Give every follower in this roster the compact Follower Card as their sheet.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.allFullHint: Return every follower in this roster to their full system sheet (spell page included).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.allCardsDone: {count} follower(s) now use the Follower Card.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.allFullDone: {count} follower(s) returned to their full sheet.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.limitHint: Maximum henchmen = 4 + CHA modifier + powers/proficiencies (RR 168). Mercenaries, specialists, and follower companions don't consume slots.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.employerModsHint: Employer modifiers applied to every hireling's effective loyalty.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.noSlot: Does not consume a henchman slot (follower apprentice/companion)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.transfer: Transfer employment (recalculates loyalty; counts as calamity, RR 163)
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.empty: No hirelings yet. Recruit some at a Location's market.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.calamityPlaceholder: e.g. missed rations, cursed, reduced to 0 hp
ACKS-HENCHMEN.roster.dismissBody: {name} leaves the roster. The actor is not deleted.

ACKS-HENCHMEN.penalty.tamperingModerate: Tampering with mortality — moderate side effect
ACKS-HENCHMEN.penalty.tamperingMajor: Tampering with mortality — major side effect

ACKS-HENCHMEN.ledger.restoreHint: Restore this adjustment — it counts toward the score again.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.ledger.compensatedTag: Compensated — no longer counts toward the score
ACKS-HENCHMEN.ledger.gmOnly: Only the Judge can compensate or restore a loyalty adjustment.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.monster.hdCap: A monster of {hd} HD cannot serve an employer of level {level} — its HD must be LOWER than the employer's level (MM 351).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.monster.animalGate: Recruiting normal animals requires Beast Friendship or Friends of Birds and Beasts (MM 351). Sapient beastmen/giants/humanoids/monstrosities/undead are open to anyone.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.monster.info: Recruiting {name} ({hd} HD — wage {wage} gp/month using HD as level, plus a half share if sapient).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.monster.feigned.betrayal: GM only: {name} only FEIGNS acceptance — it secretly loathes its employer and will betray the party when opportunity arises (Irrefusable Offer 2−).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.monster.feigned.escape: GM only: {name} only FEIGNS acceptance to save its life — it will desert at the first safe opportunity (Irrefusable Offer 3-5).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.followers.levelGate: {name} is level {level} — followers arrive at 9th level with a stronghold (RR 334).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.followers.title: Generate followers — {name}
ACKS-HENCHMEN.followers.strongholdMissin: No stronghold found (checked module APIs, flags, and inventory markers like "Stronghold: Castle"). The Judge decides whether followers arrive.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.followers.loyaltyFanatic: Fanatic followers: loyalty and morale start at +4 and they make NO loyalty rolls on calamities (morale rolls still apply).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.followers.loyaltyDefault: Followers start at loyalty +2, morale +1 over the equipment baseline.

ACKS-HENCHMEN.followers.rolled: Follower grants rolled — see the GM chat card.

ACKS-INFLUENCE.app.title: Influence
ACKS-INFLUENCE.field.targetKindHint: Detected race/kind tokens for the target (comma-separated), used to auto-apply kind-scoped bonuses (e.g. Beast Friendship vs animals) and campaign race relations. Edit to correct or clear the detection.

ACKS-INFLUENCE.effect.badge: Granted by a proficiency or active effect on the character.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.unaudited.badge: Unverified: these mechanics were classified automatically from the book text, not checked against the page. The sign or the conditions may be wrong — it is offered unticked, and the printed text governs.

ACKS-INFLUENCE.hidden.field: Hidden — you can't see this target's sheet.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.hidden.total: Hidden — the total and result are whispered to the GM; you'll see only the resulting attitude.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.hidden.sentToGm: Influence roll sent to the GM to resolve against the hidden target.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.hidden.noGm: No GM is online to resolve a roll against this hidden target.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.band.seduction.2: Hostile, attacks or calls for aid
ACKS-INFLUENCE.chat.bewitched: total is 12+ — the subject acts bewitched while in the character's presence.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.note.intimTemporary: Intimidation is temporary — make a new reaction roll if the character encounters new allies of the intimidated creature, or the conditions materially change.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.note.intimidated: Intimidated: withdraws or escapes at the first opportunity (otherwise acts Indifferent); treated as Neutral for Diplomacy and Seduction; if combat begins, it starts faltering.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.note.overawed: Overawed: acts as if Friendly while intimidated; treated as Neutral for Diplomacy and Seduction; if combat begins, it starts frightened.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.note.bribeCrime: Unmodified 2 — the bribe was blatant enough that the character can be charged with the crime of bribery.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.note.bribeRisk: No Bribery proficiency: a failed bribe shifts the target's attitude 1 step toward Hostile.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.note.hatredDwarfGoblin: MM: dwarves revile goblins — dwarven sentries automatically have Hostile reactions to any goblins encountered (Judge's call whether it applies here).
ACKS-INFLUENCE.note.hatredGnomeKobold: MM: gnomes hold a fierce hatred for kobolds (Judge's call whether an automatic Hostile reaction applies here).
ACKS-INFLUENCE.settings.btaCaste.name: By This Axe: dwarven caste reaction modifiers
ACKS-INFLUENCE.settings.btaCaste.hint: Enable the optional BTA p.56 rule — caste-based reaction modifiers between dwarves (Highborn, Oathsworn/Craftborn/Workborn, Houseless). When off, the compendium caste effects stop contributing to rolls.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.settings.raceRelations.hi: Directional reaction modifiers between races, e.g. [{"from":"dwarf","to":"elf","value":-1,"label":"Grudge of the Vaults"}]. `from` is the influencer's race/category, `to` the target's; rows need not be symmetric. Applies to reactions, hiring, and loyalty (like Inhumanity). Modules can add rows via api.registerRaceRelations().

ACKS-INFLUENCE.mod.intimidation.fearsBos: Target fears its master more (−5 or more)

ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.hiring.title: Reaction to Hiring Offer
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.hiring.previousRefus: Previous refusals by this party (−1 each)
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.hiring.slander: Slander against the party here (−1 each)
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.hiring.refuseSlander: Refuse and slander — the party takes −1 on further reaction rolls in this town; this NPC is off-limits
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.hiring.tryAgain: Try again — sweeten the deal for another roll, else it counts as a refusal
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.loyalty.title: Hireling Loyalty
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.loyalty.hostility: Hostility — leaves service, becomes an enemy, never returns
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.loyalty.resignation: Resignation — leaves service without ill will
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.morale.title: Combat Morale
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.morale.cornered: Cannot retreat and enemy is not accepting surrender (+5)
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.morale.frightenedRet: Frightened Retreat — the creatures become frightened: they cannot attack, cast spells, or speak, and run at full speed until no longer pursued or 1d10 rounds pass. Unable to flee, they cower — and will surrender if terms are offered.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.morale.faltering: Morale Faltering — the creatures falter: −2 on attack throws, proficiency throws and saving throws versus the enemy, until they end their initiative unengaged. They will usually attempt a fighting withdrawal, and might surrender on fair terms.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.morale.fightOn: Fight On — the monsters continue the battle without retreating, but will not pursue if their opponents flee.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.morale.advancePursue: Advance and Pursue — the monsters press the attack, going on the offensive where possible, and pursue if the characters retreat.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.morale.victoryOrDeat: Victory or Death — the monsters fight on with grim determination and roll no further morale this battle. They pursue any retreating opponents.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.obedience.title: Hireling Obedience
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.obedience.refuses: Refuses — the hireling will not obey. Insisting costs 1 permanent loyalty and forces another roll.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.obedience.begrudging: Begrudging — the hireling obeys under protest: −1 on related loyalty rolls or proficiency throws, and quits early.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.irrefusable.title: Irrefusable Offer
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.irrefusable.betrayal: Betrayal — the monster feigns agreement and turns on the party at the worst moment.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.irrefusable.escape: Escape — the monster refuses and attempts to flee at the first opportunity.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.irrefusable.hesitate: Hesitates — the monster accepts reluctantly; loyalty starts at −2.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.irrefusable.accept: Accepts — the monster enters service at loyalty 0.
ACKS-INFLUENCE.mode.irrefusable.elan: Élan — the monster accepts eagerly; loyalty starts at +1.
